hypotheses: Cabozantinib's histone mark changes in A375 are driven by inhibition of multiple tyrosine kinases (e.g., MET, VEGFR2, AXL), leading to downstream chromatin remodeling. Sorafenib and regorafenib share similar kinase inhibition profiles and may produce comparable histone mark changes.

The observed histone mark changes may be due to off-target kinase inhibition (e.g., DDR1, KIT) that is not shared by all TKIs. Axitinib and dasatinib have distinct kinase selectivity and may show divergent histone effects.

The histone mark signature could be a general stress response to TKI treatment rather than a specific on-target effect. Ponatinib, with a broad kinase inhibition profile, may mimic the signature, while more selective inhibitors may not.
object.evidence_gap: No direct evidence links cabozantinib or the candidate donor drugs to the specific histone mark changes (H3K27me1K36me2, H3K9me1K14ac1, etc.) in A375 cells. The donor descriptions are pharmacological and do not provide context-specific histone perturbation data. Retrieval of donor descriptions may clarify kinase inhibition profiles but cannot confirm histone mark effects without experimental measurement.
